requirements.source_requirement: Adopt one clear leading architecture. Develop a station-powered, ferrite-PM-biased maglev with onboard suspension stabilization and guidance, station-mounted linear synchronous motors, and unpowered coasting between station zones. Keep train propulsion, magnetic support and passenger services as separate subsystems in the configuration. This preserves the requested removal of onboard main traction equipment while retaining a physically credible route to stationary hover.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Label the maturity of every parameter. Distinguish project objectives, study assumptions, candidate designs and verified requirements. Six cars and station-sourced traction are project choices; 14.2 t tare, 3 t ferrite and 8 mm clearance remain study targets. Rehberg–Blümler informs an optimization method, not validated suspension gains. The civil section now defines a 25 m repeated product, hollow support candidates, a USD 22,000 ordinary-support procurement target and a two-shift production model. Keep the 15.4 t preceding train case, 13.4 t stretch case and old civil quantities for comparison. Do not mark target geometry, cost or throughput as accepted until its evidence is attached.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Fix the Baghdad train envelope. Use six 17 m bodies, 2.65 m study width and 102 m total body length. Use 104.5 m only as an illustrative coupled footprint until couplers and gangways are resolved. Retain 120 passengers/car as the normal study loading and 160/car as the maximum study loading: 720 and 960 passengers/train, respectively, at the current 75 kg/person assumption. [R1]

requirements.amendment: User fixed-line transfer and urban/suburban spacing instructions, 21 October 2026
requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Use a 1.5 km urban spacing target minimum, approximately 2 km urban mean and explicitly classified 4–5 km suburban legs with located top-up accelerators where required. Preserve mandatory passenger-transfer junction stops and expose any shorter spacing as a conflict. Retain 1 km/90 s authored and 1 km/88 s developed cases as component benchmarks, not new route validation. The study speed limit remains 80 km/h; longer profiles require their own force, services, protection and recovery verification.
requirements.source_requirement: Keep the operating envelope explicit. Use an 80 km/h study limit. The new launch reference uses 0.8 m/s² net acceleration and service deceleration with 0.6 m/s³ jerk, a 90 s flat 1 km run and 190 s scheduled headway. Retain 0.6 and 1.0 m/s² acceleration and 100 s runtime as cost/performance alternatives. The earlier no-jerk calculations remain labelled comparisons. Route gradients, crosswinds, resistance, temperature, construction tolerances and degraded equipment remain required configuration inputs.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Remove the intended equipment from the train BOM. Delete the onboard main traction motor/windings, main traction inverter, associated traction cooling and large traction-energy battery in this variant. Retain the magnetic support/guidance hardware, its power electronics, sensors, small services battery, doors, HVAC, lighting, communications, emergency stopping/capture provision and couplers. Record the removal explicitly so that later software or mass models do not quietly restore the old propulsion arrangement.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Use magnets as the field source, not the energy source. Permanent magnets can provide magnetic bias and the field against which a station motor acts. The station electrical supply provides the train’s launch energy. Once outside a powered zone, gravity, aerodynamic resistance and magnetic losses determine the coast. A station cannot exert useful propulsion several kilometres away without powered equipment along that intervening route.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Retain active stabilization for always-hovering operation. The leading design uses attractive PM-biased suspension with corrective coils and feedback, targeting low continuous control power. More ferrite alone does not establish stable, contactless support in every direction at rest. A moving-field electrodynamic Halbach system is a different branch: its speed-dependent lift cannot simply be assumed to remain available when stopped. Normal stationary hover and an orderly support-loss response must both be demonstrated. [R2, R33]

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Use MagneMotion M3 as the closest architectural reference. Its developer report combines vehicle PM support/guidance fields, stabilization coils and wayside LSM windings. Reuse that functional arrangement as a starting point for an independent ferrite design. Its articulated pods, vehicle size, powered-guideway coverage and performance are not the OSR specification. No qualified, openly licensed six-car ferrite passenger-maglev design was identified that can simply be copied. [R2]

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Design a physically correct single-beam magnetic interface. Arrange two symmetric support interfaces around one structural beam. In the attractive configuration, vehicle pole faces must sit below the iron faces toward which they are pulled upward; a magnet above a top-mounted iron face would attract the vehicle downward. Develop the wraparound carrier, guidance faces, capture clearances and load path together. Record support and propulsion gaps explicitly, including their geometric relationship where they share a magnetic face.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Optimize finite ferrite blocks using the Rehberg–Blümler approach. Compare a conventional linear Halbach pattern with finite-block orientation optimization, an alternating-pole iron-backed circuit and a flux-concentrating ferrite/pole-piece circuit. Use the finite-dipole orientation method as an initial estimate, then optimize the actual cartridge, steel and coils in three dimensions. Preserve a useful alternating longitudinal field for propulsion as well as support force, gap tolerance and thermal/demagnetization margin. A static lift optimum need not be a useful LSM secondary. The paper’s circular-ring homogeneity gains do not establish railway lift or magnet-mass gains. [R34, R48]

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Use specific ferrite grades as comparison materials. TDK FB9B, FB9H and FB12H provide current, documented reference properties. Compare those against locally obtainable equivalents with complete demagnetization curves, dimensional tolerances and quotations. Premium performance must not be combined with an unverified commodity price. Some high-performance ferrites use lanthanum/cobalt additions; specify composition if avoiding these constituents is a procurement objective. [R3, R4]

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Check hot force and cold demagnetization separately. Use actual supplier curves over the selected temperature range, including opposing support/traction fields and faults. Ferrite remanence falls with increasing temperature, while its coercivity can become less favorable in the cold. Magnet temperature, winding hot spots and ambient air temperature are different model variables. Heat tolerance does not imply constant lift or unlimited service life for adhesives, insulation and seals. [R5, R6]

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Retain 3 t of ferrite for the first optimized-cartridge comparison. At 5,000 kg/m³ this is 0.60 m³/car, or 18 t/train. The user’s USD 7,000/car assumption is USD 2.33/kg and USD 42,000/train for raw ferrite. Compare orientations at identical volume before shrinking the array. A conditional constant-performance resizing calculation gives about 2.85 t/car with the lighter central body, but requires the original force-per-mass premise to be demonstrated. Keep grade, machining, magnetization, keyed retention, inspection and assembly costs separate.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Start with 24 support cartridges per car. At the revised 26.2 t maximum study load, weight is approximately 257.0 kN/car, or 10.71 kN/cartridge with equal static sharing. Three tonnes of ferrite averages 125 kg/cartridge. Develop 12 paired support stations along the car as a layout seed, resolving their real pitch and distance from car ends in CAD. Uneven passengers, structural flexibility, pitch/roll, beam joints and failed channels determine the higher local ratings; equal division is only a static screen.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Use magnetic pressure as a sanity check. The ideal relation p = B²/(2μ₀) requires approximately 0.232 T equivalent gap field to support 257.0 kN over 12 m² of effective pole area. An illustrative 1.3 force multiplier raises that to 0.265 T. These are required-performance checks, not solved magnetic designs. Remanence is not useful gap field. A hypothetical 2.8% gain in gap field at unchanged area gives about 5.7% more ideal pressure; the Rehberg–Blümler ring result does not establish that gain for this rail.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Optimize the whole empty-to-loaded force envelope. The 14.2 t tare and 26.2 t loaded cases require a force ratio of 1.845, while the payload force swing remains 117.7 kN/car. Under the ideal same-area relationship, empty support requires about 73.6% of the full-load gap field. Biasing the PM circuit at full load could therefore require substantial opposing trim when empty. Compare mid-load bias, controlled gap adjustment and coil authority using force–gap–current–temperature maps. A flatter force–gap curve improves disturbance tolerance but accommodates less payload change through a few millimetres of travel. Retain active stabilization, boarding tolerances and fault margins.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Optimize the gap with the civil works. Compare 8, 12, 16 and 20 mm support clearances wherever the magnetic circuit can operate. First spend any validated magnetic improvement on lower complete system cost: potentially more alignment margin, lower trim losses or less material. These benefits compete and must be measured. Larger gaps can require more magnetic material or power. Retain separate budgets for manufacture, installation, body/beam motion, temperature, control error, curves and capture; optimize both the train and guideway.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Resolve the rigid-carrier curvature problem early. For a straight 12 m magnetic footprint, the chord-height difference L²/(8R) is 18 mm at a 1,000 m vertical radius, 6 mm at 3,000 m and 3.6 mm at 5,000 m. These are significant against an 8 mm gap. Short cartridges rigidly attached to one straight frame do not remove the problem. Either constrain geometry or explicitly permit limited compliant/articulated carriers.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Integrate carriers into reinforced body load paths. Locate magnetic hardpoints on continuous longitudinal members and local sandwich reinforcements, sharing brackets and load spreaders where analysis permits. Keep brittle ferrite positively retained inside replaceable cartridges; it cannot carry primary body tension, bending, coupler or crash loads. Use an interface BOM to prevent omission or double-counting between the GFRP body’s hardpoints and the separate magnetic-carrier allowance. Include joint creep, local peel, thermal expansion and repair access. [R7]

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Close guidance, damping and capture as distinct functions. Evaluate lateral restoring force, roll, pitch, yaw and damping over the full running envelope. Size guidance channels for wind, curves, uneven loads and disturbances. Add a normally clear capture/landing interface and a defined degraded condition. Do not count passive centering as demonstrated dynamic stability, or assign all emergency hardware to an unexplained mass allowance.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Optimize the passive rail jointly with the magnets. Compare laminated or appropriately insulated/segmented iron interfaces, including fasteners, return paths and joints. The current quantity model contains about 300 kg of rail steel per guideway-metre, making this a major cost target. Greater useful flux can require more return-path steel if saturation controls, so improved magnet orientation does not automatically justify a thinner rail. Compare measured force, saturation, pole-passing eddy/hysteresis drag and finished installed cost. Study 0.35 and 0.5 mm electrical-steel lamination classes where appropriate; the assembled rail thickness is a separate dimension. [R8, R32]

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Co-design pole pitch with the entire consist. Compare 0.10, 0.20, 0.25 and 0.30 m pole pitches. The 0.25 m seed gives a 0.50 m electrical wavelength, about 44.4 Hz at 80 km/h and 30.8 Hz at the new 55.4 km/h launch speed. An illustrative 17.5 m car pitch then equals 35 complete wavelengths, allowing identical car arrays to share phase. Other pitches require deliberate magnetic indexing or separate phase control. Include coupler motion, actual array datums, end effects and slotting; frequency alone does not select the design.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Build a three-phase iron-core station LSM from repeated cassettes. Use a 2.5 m mechanical cassette per face as the new factory seed, paired across the two interfaces. Five paired sets form a 12.5 m addressable section; two sections match a 25 m civil span. Compare distributed windings and concentrated coils using actual cost, force ripple and end effects. Develop shared support/thrust ferrite first as an integration objective, with a separately measured propulsion coupon for characterization. Separate production propulsion magnets must be charged to vehicle mass and cost, not assumed to fit the existing 3 t/car allocation.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Model support, thrust and electrical loading simultaneously. Produce force/moment, flux-linkage, resistance, inductance and loss maps versus position, gap, overlap, phase current, electrical angle and temperature. Evaluate launch, braking, unpowered stator passage and inverter faults. Include reactive current and voltage headroom. If shared fields demand substantial suspension trim, revise the support-power and battery budgets. More force per metre may shorten the winding while increasing copper, converter, normal-force and cooling cost.

requirements.amendment: User fixed-line transfer and urban/suburban spacing instructions, 21 October 2026
requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Compare and price finite station and booster winding lengths and fixed groups against qualified sectioned supplies. A longer station gap cannot reuse a 200 m winding without an overlap/force/voltage check. Include phase-correct section handover and inactive-stator faults; no physical acceptance is implied by offline replay.
requirements.source_requirement: Compare fixed winding groups before a switching matrix. Price one 200 m fixed winding per lane, two approximately 100 m groups per lane, and 12.5 m sections routed to a few inverter channels. Start detailed circuit design with the two-group arrangement: four independently controlled bridges per two-direction station, common DC infrastructure and no output selector matrix. Actual R/L, back EMF and current duty must decide the winner. The short-section variant requires phase-correct, current-free transfer and available thrust during handover. Keep a station LIM with a passive vehicle aluminum secondary as a separately costed fallback. [R2, R9, R49, R50]

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Size station power from the jerk-limited loaded trajectory. The reference six-car 157.2 t case requires 134.15 kN peak thrust, 1.994 MW peak mechanical propulsion and 5.501 kWh launch work. At a provisional 85% aggregate efficiency these become 2.346 MW and 6.472 kWh input, before services. Receiving braking peaks at 1.437 MW mechanical. These real-power figures do not establish bridge current or kVA rating. Every installed group/channel must be priced, including inactive hardware and required redundancy.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Use partial overlap to reduce station winding length. The reference launch and brake travel are 159.81 and 108.16 m. Keeping the full 104.5 m train engaged throughout would require 372.47 m winding per direction. With six assumed 12 m active magnet bands and 4 kN per metre of equivalent train-envelope overlap, the optimized minimum is 185.66 m. Study 200–225 m after module rounding and margin; the 200 m geometry does not provide a full 20% force reserve in both phases. These are conditional force-overlap results, requiring motor, voltage, thermal and fault validation. Count both directions and both motor faces.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Use one auditable longitudinal model. The central flat case uses 26,200 kg/car, six cars and R(v) = 1,000 + 1.8v² N/car with v in m/s. Integrate jerk-limited launch, zero-thrust coast and receiving braking; solve launch and brake-entry speeds for the required distance/time. Retain the earlier 27,400 and 25,400 kg mass comparisons. Resistance remains provisional. Replace the six-times-single-car aerodynamic approximation with a whole-consist model and measured magnetic losses before route acceptance.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Preserve the earlier profiles as explicitly limited comparisons. The following historical screening table uses a = d = 1 m/s² and omits jerk ramps and dwell. It remains useful for tracing the earlier mass revision, but the new Station launch design section supplies the current jerk-limited operating and hardware study. Mechanical launch work excludes converter losses; receiving brake work is the mechanical energy absorbed by the station motor. The near-natural-stop row is a mathematical comparison, not a berthing method.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Minimize total energy and complete service cost. For the new 90 s reference, moving hot services consume 9 kWh/train; launch input at 85% adds 6.472 kWh, totaling about 15.47 kWh before dwell and station losses. A 100 s reference reduces launch input to 5.00 kWh but raises moving services to 10 kWh, totaling about 15.00 kWh. The small combined saving must be weighed against journey time, headway and hardware. Retain the older energy figures only with their no-jerk profile labels. Lower body mass does not itself reduce passenger HVAC demand.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Include gradients and inertia in the coasting calculation. The central loaded car launched at 80 km/h coasts about 4.63 km to rest on the level, or 1.62 km on a continuous 1% uphill, under the assumed resistance law. The corresponding earlier level result was 4.84 km. Lower inertia means faster slowing under unchanged drag, so lower mass does not by itself extend coasting range. A 1% uphill adds 2.57 kN/car. Optimize magnetic losses, aerodynamic resistance, station elevation and route curvature explicitly; downhill can require positive braking.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Plan a robust arrival window. Optimize launch energy for measured mass, timetable, wind, resistance, voltage and route profile. Require adequate speed on entry to the receiving motor zone under the high-resistance case and adequate stopping capacity under the low-resistance/downhill case. Let the receiving station provide a small corrective push or brake. Exact zero-energy arrival under one nominal model is too sensitive to be the operating rule.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Use station resistor braking as the baseline. The receiving LSM generates into the station DC bus; a chopper and resistor absorb energy without an onboard traction battery or export to the grid. In the new reference, an assumed 85% generating efficiency gives about 1.22 MW peak into the bus and 2.81 kWh / 10.13 MJ per arrival. At 180 s headway that averages 56.3 kW heat per direction. Size pulse power, repeated energy, ambient cooling, coincidence and failure response. Direct DC-bus energy reuse is optional; stopping must remain available without an energy consumer. [R50]

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Provide an independent stopping and holding function. A receiver can fail after the departure station has committed the train. Examine independent arrival-brake channels, fail-operational station supply, and an onboard emergency stopping/holding mechanism with passive reaction surfaces where necessary. Eddy-current braking alone cannot hold a stationary train. Cutting electrical propulsion also does not stop a train already coasting. Select the complete degraded-mode architecture before removing all mechanical emergency components.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Define the moving-parts objective precisely. Target no wheels, gearboxes, rotating traction motors or mechanical transmissions in normal operation, and minimize articulated support hardware where geometry permits. Doors, HVAC fans/compressors, couplers, charging interfaces and emergency deployment hardware still have motion. Do not optimize a literal “zero moving parts” label at the expense of larger route radii, expensive alignment or impractical recovery.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Make a structurally participating GFRP sandwich body the leading study. Use repeated flat or gently curved panels, continuous longitudinal load paths, reinforced openings and concentrated hardpoints. Compare vacuum infusion and light RTM with local production capability, cure control and fleet volume. Keep metallic fittings or local substructures where they efficiently handle coupler, suspension and lifting reactions. Avoid retaining a complete conventional frame underneath non-structural cladding if claiming the central mass saving. Rail composite demonstrators support this construction direction, while OSR’s sections and joints require their own sizing. [R35, R36]

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Specify a complete laminate, core and joint system. The central takeoff uses 1,900 kg/m³ GFRP faces, an 80 kg/m³ upper-shell core and a 100 kg/m³ floor core. These are property targets, not qualified material selections. Compare rail-oriented AIREX T90 and higher-temperature R82 core families with other suppliers, including PET-core alternatives. Qualify faces, core, adhesive, coatings and liners together for hot strength, creep, fire/smoke and repair. Catalogue core temperature or fire claims do not qualify the finished body. Standardize mold families, inserts, scarf/lap joints and inspection. [R36–R41]

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Adopt 14.2 t/car as the central mass target with visible reserve. The equipped GFRP body is budgeted at 5.2 t, including a 3.2 t structural shell plus doors, glazing, interior and extra treatments. Retain 3.0 t ferrite and the full 1.8 t growth reserve. This gives 85.2 t/train empty and 157.2 t at maximum study load. Use 15.3 t/car as a conservative GFRP case and 13.4 t/car as a stretch case. The 1.5 t magnetic-equipment allocation still needs physical sizing; chute equipment and other missing details must be itemized and charged to equipment or reserve. The detailed body takeoff follows the numbered list.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Size the battery from the service mission. Study 20, 30 and 40 kWh/car. At 100 Wh/kg packaged, these are 200, 300 and 400 kg. Applying 80% end-of-life capacity and a 60% operating SOC window leaves 9.6, 14.4 and 19.2 kWh. At 60 kW/car, these correspond to the same numbers of minutes before journey consumption and protected reserve. The reserve must follow the actual recovery and emergency-service mission.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Include charging as a major station load. A 90 s hot trip consumes 9 kWh/train. Replacing it in 45 s requires 720 kW charging before losses; direct dwell services add 360 kW, giving 1.08 MW per berthed train. Charging over 60 s gives 540 + 360 = 900 kW. A 30 kWh/car pack must prove repeated 4C or 3C charging, respectively, in the specified thermal and ageing envelope. Compare actual contact/inductive interfaces, charger efficiency, life, cooling and battery mass. Longer charging dwell consumes throughput.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Engineer HVAC and insulation together. Retain 40 kW/car normal and 60 kW/car hot total services as provisional budgets that already include support/guidance and auxiliaries. Integrate sandwich-core insulation and thermal breaks, then calculate glazing, solar gain, occupants, fresh air, door cycling, filtration and fouling. Release smaller HVAC or battery allowances only from the service-duty model. The body’s lower mass alone is insufficient. Use a replaceable electric package; SUTRAK ACE235 remains a packaging reference rather than a selected Baghdad rating. [R13]

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Treat roof solar as an optional service offset. A 17 m by 2.65 m roof has 45.05 m² gross area. At an illustrative 1 kW/m² irradiance and 20% conversion, complete coverage would produce about 9 kW peak/car, before temperature and system losses. Actual area is smaller after HVAC, access and clearances. Compare shading/insulation benefits and maintenance costs; do not use solar to guarantee nighttime hover or full hot-day HVAC.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Make door assumptions consistent with capacity and body mass. The GFRP takeoff initially assumes four 1.40 m by 2.10 m passenger openings per car, two on each side, with complete mechanisms budgeted separately from the shell. Validate that arrangement against six-car dwell, passenger distribution and evacuation. Increasing the number or width of doors changes openings, reinforcement, mechanisms, platform interfaces and mass. Maintain level accessible boarding, door interlocks, handholds and emergency communication over the suspension/load range.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Make couplers and magnet phase one interface requirement. Include structural/electrical interfaces, gangways, articulation, rescue and crash load paths. For a 0.50 m magnetic wavelength, 5 mm longitudinal error is 3.6 electrical degrees and 25 mm is 18 degrees. Successive coupler deflections can accumulate along six cars. Qualify per-car magnet origins, coupler travel/stiffness and load-dependent phase. A common travelling field requires coherent registration; a section overlapping two differently phased cars cannot control their phases independently merely because the section has its own inverter.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Make the composite and magnetic assembly sequence explicit. Each panel and cartridge needs part/revision identity, mass/CG, lifting and support points, datums, joining/fastening process, access and inspection limits. Plan mold preparation, layup, cure, trimming, joint preparation, insert installation and geometry checks before equipment fitting. Use keyed magnet pockets and handling fixtures to control polarity and attraction forces. Track actual resin uptake, process yield and labor hours; intended simplicity must appear in the work instructions and purchasing quantities.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.requirement: Prioritize achievable local manufacture. Candidate local work includes precast concrete, fabricated frames, panel production, structural carriers, winding assembly, wiring harnesses, final assembly and test. Procure ferrite, electrical steel, semiconductors, qualified cells, bearings and specialist components through interchangeable specifications where feasible. Eliminating a proprietary bogie supplier changes the supply chain; it does not eliminate the need for qualified suppliers and controlled processes.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.implementation_owner: Rust station launch/support contracts; offline replays
requirements.requirement: Implement the proposed departure rule as an exclusive reservation. Launch only when the preceding train has completely cleared the receiving station and protective boundary, the interstation corridor is clear, and the next berth is available. Atomically reserve corridor, receiving berth and required overlap for the named train. Also prove receiving braking, train health, services reserve, door closure and route readiness before launch.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.implementation_owner: Rust station launch/support contracts; offline replays
requirements.requirement: Use a small explicit resource state machine. Use states such as available, reserved, occupied, release pending, blocked and unknown, with train ownership and configuration identity. Lost communications or expired permission must not make a resource available. Release needs positive, sufficiently current full-clearance evidence. Model delayed/replayed messages, restarts, inconsistent sensors and failed departure; a timer alone never proves that a coasting train has disappeared.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.implementation_owner: Rust station launch/support contracts; offline replays
requirements.requirement: Reuse the repository’s persistent locks. The existing resources.rs and resource_log.rs already make locks outlive permissions and require clearance evidence. Extend that machinery for the station launch transaction rather than writing a parallel interlocking. The conventional three-second movement-authority window in ma.rs needs distinct launch/commit semantics: permission may expire before departure, but expiry after launch cannot release the corridor or command physically impossible immediate stopping. [R14]

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.implementation_owner: Rust station launch/support contracts; offline replays
requirements.requirement: Detect the complete consist. Use a qualified non-contact boundary-detection and train-integrity method suited to a wheel-free vehicle. A front-end detection or expected travel time is insufficient. Establish tail-clear position and margins, including a separated or failed car. Conventional wheel/axle detectors cannot simply be assumed available on this vehicle. Retain monitoring during the coast for abnormal occupancy and train condition.

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.implementation_owner: Rust station launch/support contracts; offline replays
requirements.requirement: Use an STM32 for a bounded local control task. STM32G4/H7-class hardware can prototype current loops, PWM and local position acquisition. ST documents FOC support; SimpleFOC provides an MIT-licensed algorithm reference. Neither is a complete railway controller. Retain independent launch/brake authority and hardware protection. At 0.25 m pole pitch, 5 electrical degrees corresponds to 6.94 mm, traversed in 0.347 ms at 20 m/s. Use timestamped/predicted local phase, calibrated sensors and absolute section identity; back EMF alone supplies no zero-speed phase. [R15, R51–R53]

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
requirements.implementation_owner: Rust station launch/support contracts; offline replays
requirements.requirement: Keep GoA4 functions beyond separation in scope. Fixed station blocks can simplify traffic separation. Door control, precise berthing, obstacle response, passenger communication, train health, emergency handling, degraded operation and recovery still need an allocated design. ORR’s unattended-operation principles are a useful engineering checklist, not an automatic statement of Iraqi legal applicability. Define the project’s applicable standards and assurance responsibilities with the relevant authority. [R16]

requirements.digital_scope: Implemented bounded study or allocated interface; detailed/physical qualification remains open
